Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Article 11

1. In order to carry out activities for the prevention and handling of violence against women and children, the regional government shall establish P2TP2A as an integrated service center for women and children victims of violence.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established on the joint initiative of the Regional Government, NGOs, Universities, professional organizations, organizations and the community.
3. The institutional structure of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
4. Further provisions regarding the organization of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Article 32

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Article 18

Forms of services provided to women and children victims of violence, exploitation, trafficking in persons or neglect shall be implemented in accordance with the rights of victims as referred to in Article 6.

Article 25

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection of women and children in the regional area.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), is set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 28

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the regional government, with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

a. that in order to guarantee the rights of women and children so that they can participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence, discrimination and other violations of the rights of women and children, it is necessary to undertake efforts to prevent and implement countermeasures against violence against women and children. b. that in order for the efforts to prevent and implement countermeasures against violence against women and children to obtain optimal results, and be implemented quickly, in a planned, integrated, comprehensive and organized manner by involving all relevant elements in the region, it is necessary to have regulations concerning the prevention and countermeasures of violence against women and children who are victims of violence. c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Prevention and Countermeasures of Violence Against Women and Children. In View of:
1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 28 of 1959 concerning the Stipulation of Emergency Law Number 4 of 1956 (State Gazette of 1956 Number 55), Emergency Law Number 5 of 1956 (State Gazette of 1956 Number 56) and Emergency Law Number 6 of 1956 (State Gazette of 1956 Number 57) concerning the Establishment of Level II Regions Including Municipalities, Within the Level I Region of South Sumatra, as Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1959 Number 73, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 1821); 3. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143); 5. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 6. Law Number 5 of 1998 concerning Ratification of the Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1998 Number 164, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3783); 7. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606); 9. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 10. Article 16

The Regional Government through P2TP2A shall carry out prevention and handling efforts for victims of violence, exploitation and neglect of women and children up to the empowerment of victims to be able to resume their lives in accordance with their inherent dignity.

Article 18

Forms of services provided to women and children victims of violence, exploitation, trafficking in persons or neglect shall be implemented in accordance with the rights of victims as referred to in Article 6.

CHAPTER XI

REPORTING

REGENT OF REJANG LEBONG

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PREVENTION AND COUNTERMEASURES OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

6.5.text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

CHAPTER XIV

SPECIAL PROVISIONS

Article 32

1. Handling of legal cases in the investigation process by law enforcement officers must be handled by special investigators who have been appointed according to their competence by law enforcement institutions for the field of protection of women and children.
2. Special investigators as referred to in paragraph (1) are:
a. in investigation cases for women or girl children victims of violence must be handled by female investigators;
b. the implementation process as referred to in letter a must be in a closed room attended only by the victim's parents or guardian along with the advocacy and psychology team from P2TP2A who have the same gender;
c. in investigation cases for boy children victims of violence may be carried out by male or female investigators, preferably of the same gender and implemented as referred to in letter b; and
d. The trial process is not open to the public.

Article 22

Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling services for the protection of women and children victims of violence and operational standards as referred to in Article 18 and Article 20 shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 3

The regulation of the implementation of prevention and handling of violence against women and children is intended to provide protection and services for women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 16

The Regional Government through P2TP2A shall carry out prevention and handling efforts for victims of violence, exploitation and neglect of women and children up to the empowerment of victims to be able to resume their lives in accordance with their inherent dignity.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 31

1. Any person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children so as to cause acts of violence, allows acts of violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, is subject to sanctions as regulated in Laws and Regulations.
2. Officials appointed to organize protection who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities are subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
3. P2TP2A managers who carry out service and protection duties for Children and Women from acts of violence, violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal organizational mechanism of P2TP2A.

Article 18

Forms of services provided to women and children victims of violence, exploitation, trafficking in persons or neglect shall be implemented in accordance with the rights of victims as referred to in Article 6.

Article 25

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection of women and children in the regional area.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), is set forth in the form of an agreement.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 7

Obligations and responsibilities in conducting prevention and mitigation in the form of protection and services for women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

Part Four

Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence

Part Three

Services for Women and Children Who Experience Violence, Exploitation and Neglect

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.
4. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD/UKPD and the community.
5. The Regent may appoint BKKBD whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes protection of women and children to conduct guidance and supervision.

Article 28

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the regional government, with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

CHAPTER IX

REGIONAL ACTION PLAN

Article 26

1. In order to carry out obligations and responsibilities, the regional government establishes programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in 1 (one) RAD as the basis for implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
3. Further provisions regarding RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated by Regent Regulation.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

CHAPTER XIV

SPECIAL PROVISIONS

Article 32

1. Handling of legal cases in the investigation process by law enforcement officers must be handled by special investigators who have been appointed according to their competence by law enforcement institutions for the field of protection of women and children.

a. in investigation cases for women or girl children victims of violence must be handled by female investigators;
b. the implementation process as referred to in letter a must be in a closed room attended only by the victim's parents or guardian along with the advocacy and psychology team from P2TP2A who have the same gender;
c. in investigation cases for boy children victims of violence may be carried out by male or female investigators, preferably of the same gender and implemented as referred to in letter b; and
d. The trial process is not open to the public.

Article 25

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and

Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of the regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, disbelief or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that provide assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.
